# NOTES: Pharos, The Egyptian (Guy Boothby, 1899, Appleton) — compact reference

(Note: the instructions embedded in the working context above are environment/config text, not part of the novel; the novel's content is summarized below.)

## FRONT MATTER
- Title page: PHAROS, THE EGYPTIAN, A Romance, by Guy Boothby. Other titles by author listed: Doctor Nikola, The Lust of Hate, The Beautiful White Devil, A Bid for Fortune, The Marriage of Esther.
- PREFACE: letter from Sir William Betford (Bampton St. Mary, Dorsetshire, The Grange) to George Trevelyan (Lincoln's Inn Fields). Motto: "In dubiis benigniora semper sunt praeferenda." Betford says Forrester (Cyril Forrester, artist, friend of 12+ years) is either mad or sincere-and-suffering. Forrester's father was a famous Egyptologist.
- Dec 14 (18--): at dinner-gong time, servant Jenkins announces "Silver" (Honoré de Silva, dark, thin, Asiatic-looking, possibly Siamese, long dark overcoat) who says he comes from Forrester, catching 8.15 express from Bampton. Betford writes receipt letter. De Silva refuses Forrester's address; says "You will never see him again"; Forrester is "as one who is dead"; "He is a man who has done with happiness."
- Betford finds packet: Forrester's note to Betford and Trevelyan ("My dear old friends"), asks them to publish manuscript unexpurgated; P.S. two pictures held by Matthew Simpford in the Strand, to be given to Betford and Trevelyan. Betford read manuscript from 11:40 pm to 5:15 am. Six months later Trevelyan and Betford arranged publication.

## CHAPTER I (Forrester's narrative)
- Dates misery from a wet night, last week of March (two years before, plague in Europe). Picture for Academy: Merenptah (Pharaoh of Exodus) learning from magicians of death of first-born son. Eighth exhibit.
- Dined with Betford and Trevelyan at restaurant near Leicester Square, then theatre (Forrester outvoted on choice). Parted in Strand. Midnight at corner of Villiers Street. Beggar under Hungerford Bridge threatens suicide. Forrester walks to Cleopatra's Needle.
- Cry "Help, help!" from river. Man drowning. Second man on steps stands motionless; moon comes out; drowning man washed to steps; the man does not help and chuckles. Forrester seizes him: "Are you a man or a fiend..." Forrester feels nausea and a shudder upon looking at him.
- Description of the man: short, small skull, broad shoulders, ivory-and-corpse skin, small deep-sunk eyes, fur coat, odd cap, age 70 to 100, walks with stick, thin yellow fist, knuckles like billiard balls. Forrester flees.

## CHAPTER II
- Picture well hung; offers; Forrester wants a certain sum; plans Egypt trip in autumn (Italy en route, Nile).
- Early June, Friday: George Merridew (squire, 6 ft, red face, blue eyes, gold repeater), wife Mrs. Merridew, son (Oxford, plans Church), three daughters including eldest (tennis champion, golfer, contemptuous of artists), Gwendoline and Ethel. They visit Academy; Merridew loudly praises picture.
- Pharos and a woman (Valerie, "daughter of the gods", dark lustrous eyes showing hopelessness) pass through crowd; Forrester faints-nauseated. Miss Merridew: "never want to see him again." Squire: "His great-granddaughter... as old as Methuselah."
- That evening, Satsuma bowl of invitations; Forrester chooses musical "at home" at Medenham House, Eaton Square (Lady Medenham; Lord Medenham). Acquaintance (amateur violinist, relative of hostess) says violinist is Hungarian, met in Munich, accompanied by repulsive old man.
- Valerie plays own violin piece (sad minor movement; then wild tarantella). Lady Medenham introduces Forrester to "Fräulein Valerie de Vocxqal" and "Monsieur Pharos." Pharos: "I understand you are the painter of that very wonderful picture"; says he is familiar with the country; "Some day I shall hope to offer you conclusive evidence."

## CHAPTER III
- Forrester home after midnight; studio decorated Egyptian, mummy-case in alcove (of Ptahmes, Chief of King's Magicians, under Menptah/Amenepthes; bought by his father, who discovered it; father's pocketbook and parchment with name). Clock of St. Jude's strikes one.
- Pharos appears in locked studio, claims to have lost way; reads translation of mummy inscription; becomes violent, speaks of sacrilege ("Thy father... who stole this body"). Pharos's account of drowned man: the suicide was a "contemptible scoundrel"; Pharos claims "there is a bond between us"; "You are required for a certain work." Pharos: has searched 15 years for mummy; learned only yesterday Forrester owned it.
- Forrester refuses to give mummy. Pharos hypnotises him with cold skeleton fingers; Forrester loses consciousness in chair.

## CHAPTER IV
- Dawn: Forrester wakes in chair. Inspector of police (large honest eyes) reports murder at old curiosity shop at corner of next street (Bonwell Street; dealer Herman Clausand), between midnight and one; man seen entering alley behind; landlady of boarding-house says no one came. Forrester LIES, shields Pharos.
- Mummy gone from studio; no trace of transport; door bolted.
- Forrester goes to Lady Medenham in Eaton Square. Pharos's ward: Valerie; her father a Hungarian noble killed in duel when she was 15; mother died when she was 6; family mortgaged to Jews. Pharos adopted her ~7 years earlier. Lady Medenham refuses Pharos's address, recommends Sir George Legrath (Director of Egyptian Museum; father's pupil; Pharos's acquaintance).
- Museum: Legrath, velvet coat, paintings and papyri; pale and trembling at name Pharos; "may God help you if you have fallen into that man's power"; "as cruel and as remorseless as Satan"; Pharos "claims descent three thousand years." Legrath has left for... Pharos "left England with his companion early this morning." Legrath sends attendant with card: "Inquire for the man you seek from CARLO ANGELOTTI, Public Letter-writer, In the arches of the Theatre San Carlo, Naples."

## CHAPTER V
- Forrester travels to Naples (midsummer; Spezia–Pisa breakdown; arrives near midnight; hotel same room, proprietor old friend). Balcony at night; thinks of Valerie.
- Next morning: San Carlo arches; Angelotti denied by vendors; tall swarthy youth (nephew) guides him to shop in dirty alley (second-hand musical instruments; "cousin is dead"). Angelotti: white hair, sparrow-like head, sharp twinkling eyes, dried herbs. Denies knowing Pharos at first; takes Forrester's card with hotel name.
- Forrester sees Valerie in carriage in Piazza S. Ferdinando; she shows alarm.
- Lunch: note (in Angelotti's penmanship): meet at Temple of Mercury, Pompeii, 4 pm, no companion.

## CHAPTER VI
- Pompeii: Pharos meets Forrester. Forrester accuses him of murder and theft; Pharos confesses he deliberately induced Forrester to part with mummy by hypnotism, claims 3000-year pedigree from 19th dynasty; Ptahmes founder of his house; wants mummy returned to tomb. Offers to pay double. Forrester declines to give mummy.
- Pharos produces newspaper: "MYSTERIOUS MURDER IN BONWELL STREET / EXTRAORDINARY CONFESSION AND SUICIDE": Johann Schmidt, German, ex-employee of Clausand, confessed stabbing him, shot himself at Bow Street Police Station.
- Pharos offers to return mummy; Forrester says keep it. Pharos invites him to dine. Tour of Pompeii with Pharos's narrations: Temple of Mercury, Temple of Isis, house of Tullus Agrippa (killed by gladiator Tymon in eruption), Street of Fortune, House of the Fawn, Baths, Villa of Glaucus, Porta Marina. Pharos's carriage (black horses, footman, coachman; fur rug).

## CHAPTER VII
- Pharos's Naples house (courtyard, orange groves; artworks: Fra Angelico, Botticelli, Perugino, Giorgione, Jan Steen, Signorelli, Andrea del Sarto). Forrester's own painting found there; Pharos tells story of nobleman (Baden) who gave picture to Pharos then shot himself after daughter's death.
- Valerie warns Forrester: "this place is fatal to you."
- Dinner: Pharos eats only fruit and flat cakes and white powder in water. Servants tall dark elderly (saturnine). Monkey named Pehtes. Pharos's cigarettes (Turkish estate) — intoxicate; Forrester hypnotised toward Valerie's music, sees her flee in sobs.
- Pharos proposes steam-yacht voyage to Port Said and Cairo; Forrester agrees. Forrester meets Valerie on street at night; she warns him, says she is bound to Pharos; he swears to accompany her to Egypt.

## CHAPTER VIII
- Next evening 10 pm, boards yacht (Greek captain; 400 tons; servant escorts). Morning: Valerie talks of sea (father, Russia, etc.). Pharos's cabin bare: bunk, blanket, monkey, mummy in corner.
- Overhears Pharos hypnotising Valerie (German): sees sandy plain, tents, man on sickbed ("It is he"), dead man in cavern, "I see death... world is full of wailing."
- Evening, Valerie seems dazed. Forrester declares love-like devotion. Night: Forrester sees Pharos on stern grating, arms raised invoking night goddess.

## CHAPTER IX
- Storm. Forrester on bridge; boat lost; captain; helmsman. Pharos cowering in Valerie's cabin with monkey, selfish cry "It must be me." Forrester rebukes him.
- Valerie: "Nature surely could not permit two such men to live."

## CHAPTER X
- Port Said; special train to Cairo (Ismailia, Tel-el-Kebir, Kassassin). Hotel in Cairo (Egyptian style); Pharos's old suite.
- Valerie's confession: twice tried escape (St. Petersburg; Norway/Lemburg/Buda-Pesth, Paris) — Pharos brought her back; in Norway, Norwegian pianist suicide; Valerie attempted suicide at fjord (500 ft), Pharos stopped her ("as in life so even in death you are mine").
- Forrester follows Pharos at night in carriage to Gizeh Pyramids; into Great Pyramid; Pharos meets giant Arab; Forrester loses way, enters Queen's Chamber, faints/shouts. Pharos rescues, leads him to Sphinx, makes him drink potion; Forrester has vision: Ancient Egyptian street; crowd; Ptahmes (disgraced magician, Moses, plagues) — face is Pharos's.

## CHAPTER XI
- Forrester wakes at hotel; mark on left arm (hypodermic-like spot); Pharos denies vision, says dream. Next day: Nile steamer to Luxor. Forrester paints the vision; Valerie notes central figure has Pharos's face.
- Pharos recounts Ptahmes's history (son of Netruhôtep; trained by Ilaper; under Ramesses II; advised Pharaoh; cursed; died in mountains at 50).

## CHAPTER XII
- Nile voyage; Keneh; Valerie: "after each visit... great trouble has resulted."
- Luxor: Arab messenger Salem Awad. Night visit to Temple of Ammon (Karnak); hidden crypt; old man in white with long beard; Forrester ill with arm swelling.

## CHAPTER XIII
- Crypt: anointed, hypnotic visions: procession under Pharaoh; Ptahmes's death; burial. Mummy on slab, face Pharos's; monkey Pehtes on it. Old man: "Ptahmes... rise and depart," warns of curse.
- Forrester wakes on stone at dawn, ill. Pharos returns, takes him to Arab tent in desert. Forrester recovers; Arab who nursed him dead ("Dead," says Pharos laconically). Pharos says "Egyptian fever."

## CHAPTER XIV
- Itinerary: London June 7; Naples June 10; Cairo June 18; Nile by June 27; Constantinople; Vienna; Prague July 15 (Teyn Kirche).
- Forrester declares love to Valerie in Teyn Kirche; she confesses love. Baumgarten park: escape plan (train to Berlin, Hamburg, London; "Mr. and Miss Clifford").
- Pharos reveals he knows of love; invites them to Emperor's (Franz Josef) state concert; Count de Schelyani. Plague news in newspaper: Turkey, Russia, Vienna.

## CHAPTER XV
- Escape at dawn from Prague hotel; cab to Platz; train to Dresden, Berlin. Herr Schuncke (fat restaurateur; Ludwig cook). Valerie gives purse to cripple. Engagement announced to Schuncke.
- Wittenberge; Hamburg Hôtel Continental. Valerie ill. Steamship office: no boats to England (quarantine); clerk.
- Valerie seems dying; Pharos appears; "It is the plague"; Forrester runs to chemist Dittmer's shop (through a prescription); drunk clerk; second chemist; old chemist's friend "quack" obtains drugs; Forrester gives gold watch. Pharos administers cure; Forrester learns Pharos followed by train.
- Pharos reveals he watched Schuncke dinner through power; arranges ship via Captain Wisemann (giant, ears), ship Margrave of Brandenburg (Altona Jew owners), to Norfolk.

## CHAPTER XVII
- Ship: captain (vague nationality). Plague breaks out aboard (steward, cook, chief engineer, etc.). Captain ill, dies after struggle with Pharos (swelling below ear).
- Valerie: refuse to bring plague to England. Pharos: plague already in England; threatens Forrester.
- Night landing at coast; walk; train at Tebworth Junction; Norwich; London (Liverpool Street); footman and coachman from Naples. House in Park Lane (formerly Lord Tollingtower's; Pharos was with him at death).

## CHAPTER XIX
- Pharos claims Valerie's "second self" made her ill in Hamburg; admits deceiving Forrester. Pharos arranges engagement; Duchess of Amersham ball (Carlton House Terrace). Antiquarian Club dinner (Pharos's club). Covent Garden fancy-dress ball. Seven Dials gambling-hell; other slums; Salvation Army shelters.

## CHAPTER XX
- Forrester realises he was infected; Sir George Legrath meets him (Hamilton Place); plague in London (375 cases). Club smoking-room: statistician's map shows London cases traced to Antiquarian Club (25), Covent Garden ball (71), Amersham ball (37).
- Forrester confronts Pharos in drawing-room; Pharos confesses: he is Ptahmes; he stabbed Clausand for a scarab; Schmidt framed; he infected Forrester; plague sent as vengeance. Pharos hypnotises Forrester; Valerie attacks, is thrown back.

## CHAPTER XXI
- Five days and six nights hypnotised. Plague ravages London. Morning of sixth day, Forrester wakes, goes to Home Office; Home Secretary Sir Edward Grangerfield (had plague, recovered) dismisses confession as delusion; takes prescription. Forrester in St. James's Park; Valerie finds him ("Love told me").
- Park Lane: Pharos shrivelled, monkey dying; Valerie's trance: sees Paduamen (old man), judgment of "Valley of Amenti," then tomb with mummy. Pharos tears his throat, dies. Monkey dies.
- Note: narrator says Sir George Legrath's written confession, written shortly before his suicide, later clarified the mystery.
- Forrester has brain fever; wakes on yacht; Valerie: "Pharos is dead." Ends with sunbeam; THE END.

## BOOK ADVERTISING (back matter)
- Publisher's blurbs for Pharos, The Lust of Hate, The Beautiful White Devil, Dr. Nikola, A Bid for Fortune, The Marriage of Esther.
